stories.body: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay, 85, citing her decades-long work strengthening international law and advancing accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. A former UN high commissioner for human rights, judge on international tribunals and current International Court of Justice judge, Pillay helped establish that rape and sexual violence can constitute genocide during her work on the Rwanda tribunal. The committee said the award was a defense of the rule of law at a time when international institutions face intense pressure. Pillay, who recently chaired a UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, said she initially wanted to verify the news, adding that applying the law impartially should not require courage.
stories.headline: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize

stories.body: Three Saudi nationals were killed and several people injured in two attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, Saudi authorities said, in the deadliest strike in the kingdom since a Saudi-led offensive against Yemen's Houthi rebels began the previous weekend. The Houthis claimed responsibility for targeting the airport with a ballistic missile; Saudi officials said one attack hit airport facilities and another damaged a Saudia aircraft on the ground, with no passengers aboard. Flights briefly faced disruption before airport operations resumed. The attack comes amid an escalating conflict in Yemen and wider regional tensions linked to the US-Iran war, with the Houthis advancing toward Taiz and Saudi Arabia preparing to host a major energy conference.
stories.headline: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport kills three Saudi nationals

stories.body: At least 30 people were killed after two buses carrying civilians were struck in the frontline Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk, according to Ukrainian authorities. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians and said the attack would not go unanswered. The strike, one of the deadliest in recent weeks, came as Ukrainian analysts reported battlefield setbacks for Russian forces around the northern flank of the heavily fortified Donbas cities known as the Fortress Belt, while Russian attacks continued to focus on civilian targets.
stories.headline: Russian strike on civilian buses kills at least 30 in Kramatorsk

stories.body: Ethiopian government forces launched drone strikes against Eritrean troops reported to have crossed into the northern Tigray region, raising fears that renewed fighting inside Ethiopia could expand into a regional conflict. Witnesses, a militia commander and conflict monitor ACLED said Eritrean military vehicles entered Tigray and reached Adigrat, while Ethiopian drones targeted the forces on Wednesday evening and Thursday morning. The developments follow nearly two weeks of fighting in which federal forces took the Tigrayan capital, Mekelle, from an alliance including the Tigray People's Liberation Front. Eritrea did not directly confirm its troops' presence, and tensions have been heightened by Ethiopia's push for access to the Red Sea and Eritrea's concerns about the port of Assab.
stories.headline: Ethiopia launches drone strike after Eritrean troops enter Tigray

stories.body: Isaias has strengthened into the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with sustained winds of 80 mph, and is forecast to approach the northern US Gulf Coast as a Category 2 storm. NOAA warned of life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds and widespread rainfall of 75 to 150 millimeters, with as much as 250 millimeters in some places and a risk of flash and river flooding. Hurricane warnings cover parts of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and Mississippi. A strong El Niño has contributed to an unusually quiet season; no Atlantic hurricane had formed this late in the year since 1905.
stories.headline: Hurricane Isaias becomes the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season

stories.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and wounded a man in a car in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood while a five-year-old child was inside, officials said. New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said plainclothes federal officers approached the vehicle with guns drawn as the driver was parking, after which at least one officer fired seven rounds, striking the man below his left ear. The child was unharmed. The Department of Homeland Security said the operation was intended to arrest a 28-year-old Dominican national with a criminal conviction and that the incident remains under investigation. Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the shooting and called for ICE enforcement actions in the city to end, while protests followed that evening.
stories.headline: ICE agent shoots man in New York car carrying a five-year-old

stories.body: The Trump administration has suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several large IT services companies from the PERM program, a key process through which US employers sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the system to replace US workers with lower-paid foreign labor, while Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling described widespread fraud. The move could affect thousands of workers who had been waiting for green-card applications to proceed, many of whom entered the country initially on H-1B visas. Microsoft defended its hiring practices as the administration continued a broader crackdown on both legal and undocumented immigration.
stories.headline: Trump administration blocks Microsoft from employee green-card program

stories.body: The Pentagon says the December 3 firing-squad execution of former Army Major Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, will be livestreamed. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had said the execution would be public, and a Defense Department official confirmed that it would be broadcast. Hasan would be the first person executed by the US military since 1961 and the first by military firing squad since World War II. Legal and human-rights experts said the planned broadcast raises serious questions, with the UN human rights office describing a livestreamed execution as tantamount to a public execution and potentially incompatible with the prohibition on torture.
stories.headline: Pentagon says firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed

stories.body: Republican leaders and campaign operatives are increasingly concerned that the party could lose House seats in districts Donald Trump won comfortably in 2024, according to internal polling described by Politico. The data reportedly shows competitive races in states including Iowa, Kentucky, North Carolina, Nevada, Wisconsin and Michigan, amid voter concerns about inflation, high fuel prices and the Iran war. Republicans point to fundraising advantages and a stronger ground operation, but some candidates have begun distancing themselves from Trump on issues such as tariffs, immigration and the conflict in the Middle East. A Politico poll found that one in four Trump voters believe Republican candidates should break with the president to improve their chances in November.
stories.headline: Republicans fear losses in traditionally safe House seats

stories.body: A flash poll by 40dB for El País and Cadena SER indicates that the conservative People's Party and Vox would retain an absolute parliamentary majority following Spain's early election call. The PSOE has improved its position but remains unable to close the gap between the broader progressive bloc and the right, which the survey places above 50% of voting intention and beyond the 176-seat threshold for a majority. Socialist leaders are also exploring joint left-wing Senate candidacies in up to 30 constituencies in an effort to reduce the PP's current upper-house majority ahead of the November 29 election.
stories.headline: Poll projects PP and Vox majority as Spain's early-election campaign begins

stories.body: People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has agreed to a one-on-one televised debate with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and to a four-way debate with the leading national candidates during the campaign for Spain's November 29 election. The PP proposed holding the Sánchez-Feijóo debate on November 16 through Mediaset and the four-way debate on November 26 through Atresmedia; it will also send parliamentary spokesperson Ester Muñoz to an RTVE debate involving represented parties. Feijóo declined a comparable four-way format in the 2023 campaign, making the decision a shift in strategy. He is also open to an RTVE interview, provided it is produced internally rather than by an outside production company.
stories.headline: Feijóo agrees to head-to-head debate with Sánchez and four-way televised debate

stories.body: Transport Minister Óscar Puente said Spain is not currently guaranteeing the right to decent housing and acknowledged that the government lacks the tools to resolve the housing crisis, presenting that failure as a reason for calling an early election. The comments came as the Bank of Spain warned that homebuilding is not rising fast enough to meet demand because of labor shortages, a lack of development-ready land and administrative delays. The central bank estimates a housing shortfall of roughly 750,000 homes that could approach one million within two years, despite improving financing conditions for construction and development.
stories.headline: Spanish government acknowledges it lacks tools to solve housing crisis

stories.body: National Court judge Santiago Pedraz has declined, for now, to place Spain's Socialist Party under formal investigation in the Leire Díez case, which concerns an alleged effort to obstruct judicial and police proceedings. The PP-backed popular prosecution had argued that the party should be investigated over alleged bribery, influence peddling, money laundering, embezzlement and illegal party financing. Pedraz said further investigative steps were needed because there was not yet sufficient initial evidence of structural control failures within the party or a direct or indirect benefit to it. The judge ordered further analysis of material seized from former PSOE organization secretary Santos Cerdán's home and party office.
stories.headline: Judge declines for now to charge Spain's Socialist Party in Leire Díez case

stories.body: The Bank of Spain raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 2.6% and its 2027 forecast to 2.2%, citing resilient private consumption, exports, job creation and population growth. But it also sharply increased its inflation outlook to 3.9% this year and 3.7% next year, well above the European Central Bank's 2% target. The central bank said the effects of the Middle East conflict on energy prices, including more expensive gas, oil and refining margins, have driven much of the price pressure. It expects inflation to remain near 5% late this year before easing gradually after another anticipated increase early in 2027.
stories.headline: Bank of Spain raises growth forecast but expects persistent inflation

stories.body: Barcelona has given initial approval to higher property-tax surcharges on tourist apartments from 2027, as the city moves toward eliminating tourist-flat licenses in 2028. Under the proposal, owners of one licensed tourist flat would pay a 50% surcharge on property tax, those with two to three flats would pay 100%, and owners of four or more would pay the maximum 150% surcharge. The measure was backed by the Socialist-led city government, Barcelona en Comú and ERC, opposed by the PP and Vox, and abstained on by Junts. The city expects to raise about €7 million annually and says the proceeds should support protected housing, although final approval is still required in December.
stories.headline: Barcelona moves to raise property tax on tourist flats by up to 150%

stories.body: Barcelona has launched a pilot program with three loading and unloading zones reserved for deliveries to bars, restaurants, cafés and hotels. Two sites are on Rambla del Raval in Ciutat Vella and one is at the intersection of Pau Claris and Casp in Eixample. Eight distribution companies will use a digital reservation system to coordinate delivery slots, reducing the time vehicles spend searching for space and limiting unnecessary trips through nearby streets. The trial will run for at least six months and is part of the city's goal of cutting emissions from professional mobility by 50% by 2030.
stories.headline: Barcelona pilots dedicated loading zones for hospitality deliveries

stories.body: Trains between Portbou and Barcelona resumed on Friday after five days of weather-related disruption, though some services on the R11 line were delayed by up to 30 minutes and replacement buses remained available. Passengers in Girona welcomed the return of rail service but described persistent uncertainty after days of cancellations and diversions. One traveler said she had been unable to get to work since Sunday because no viable alternative was available, while others said they could not be certain a train would run until arriving at the station. The recovery comes as Catalonia's transport network manages heavy traffic during the Pilar holiday weekend.
stories.headline: Rail service between Portbou and Barcelona resumes with delays
